text.p: Concerns over stock shortages pushed copper higher on Tuesday to fresh five-month peaks, while lead slid to a ten-month low and nickel bounced after plunging to a two-year nadir on Monday.
Copper prices finished close to the day's highs on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Tuesday, driven by another fall in stocks and global supply tightness.

Aluminium followed higher in late dealings, nickel recovered from Monday's two year lows and lead pared some of the early fund-driven losses. LME stocks fell below 100,000 tonnes for the first time since 1990 when a net 5,050 tonnes moved out on Tuesday. Three month futures responded by closing the afternoon kerb session $66 higher at $2,225 a tonne, not far from the five-month high of $2,232 hit earlier in the day.

Aluminium pushed higher, spurred on by copper's strength and a slight tightening in nearby spreads. Three month futures finished $29.50 higher at $1,464 but continued to rally after the kerb to $1,485 bid at 1735 GMT.

Nickel recovered from two-year lows posted on Monday. Stocks rose 468 tonnes, but short-covering and trade buying reversed some of Monday's declines. The market ended $240 higher at $6,860, with $7,000 seen as major resistance.

Lead fell sharply in early trade, knocked by fund liquidation after a long term rising trendline was broken. Values managed to recover back above $700 by the close, but at $703 the market was still off $14.50.
Zinc rose moderately to $1,062 from $1,058 after stocks fell 650 tonnes.
Tin gained $10 to $6,040 after stocks fell 85 tonnes.
Alloy was last indicated at $1,320/25 from $1,300/05. Stocks fell 260 tonnes.

New York precious metals futures ended lower Tuesday, as the complex drifted lower for the fourth day in a row. COMEX December gold closed down $1.30 an ounce at $378.40, after seeing a session low at $378.20. December gold saw life-of-contract lows at $377.70 on October 31. Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $377.85/378.35, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $378.20 and the New York close
Monday around $378.80/379.30. Spot gold has also found support twice since early October around $377.00 an ounce, and now looks stuck in a $377.00-385.00 range, traders said.

CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby December higher on a tight supply of deliverable wheat that has not been spoken for, traders said. There was little fresh input overnight or Tuesday. The focus was on the spreads with the December/March closing at 13-1/2 cents per bushel, premium December compared with 9-1/2 cents premium December at Monday's close. There was little input to skew the market one way or another with news

Turkey may import wheat from Argentina a possible bearish scenario. There have been hopes that Turkey soon would buy wheat from the United States. Wheat closed 3-3/4 cents per bushel higher to 4-1/2 cents lower, with December up 3-3/4 at $3.97-3/4.
Nymex crude oil prices firmed, boosted by heating oil prices hitting a session high. December crude rose 59 cents to $24.47
